description:
This allows local images to be specified by file path. It recognises paths specified using the `file:` protocol as well as relative paths with no protocol. There is a safeguard in place (which can be overridden) that prevents files being accessed from outside a “safe” path, which defaults to `./public`.

As well as enabling the more user-friendly `src={string}` interface for local files, this also means that local files will be added to react-pdf images cache just like remote ones.

comments.body: This is not necessary. You can just use global variable `BROWSER` to check if code is running on browser or not. Rollup takes care of setting it up then on build time

No need to require it here. You can use `import path from 'path'` as all other imports in this file. Rollup will ignore it for web build. Of course you should use `path` only inside a `!BROWSER` conditional

`url` is not being ignored by rollup currently but would be very easy to add.
I know it's odd for node code, but I try to keep files "isomorphic" (if that really applies here) by using ES6 imports
